lesson_title: Week 3, Lecture 4: Decision Structures (If--Elif-Else) and Boolean Logic

segments.html: So far we have been writing programs that execute one step after another. But it is often necessary to have programs that take different actions based on the data input to them. This is done with a decision structure: an "If" statement.

segments.html: For instance, in the U.S., many workers are legally entitled to extra pay if they work more than 40 hours in a week. This is often paid as "time and a half" which means that they get 1.5 times their hourly wage for every hour over 40.
segments.text: For instance, in the U.S., many workers are legally entitled to extra pay if they work more than 40 hours in a week. This is often paid as "time and a half" which means that they get 1.5 times their hourly wage for every hour over 40.

segments.html: For instance, if your hourly wage is $20, your overtime wage is $30. If you work 60 hours in a week, you earn 40 * $20 == $800 plus 20 * $30 == $600, for a total of $1400.
segments.text: For instance, if your hourly wage is $20, your overtime wage is $30. If you work 60 hours in a week, you earn 40 * $20 == $800 plus 20 * $30 == $600, for a total of $1400.

hours=float(input("How many hours did you work last week?"))
wage=float(input("What was your hourly wage?"))
if (hours>40.0):
  # calculate non-overtime and overtime pay
  non_overtime=40*wage
  overtime=(hours-40)*(wage*1.5)
if (hours<=40.0):
  # otherwise no overtime
  non_overtime=hours*wage
  overtime=0
total_pay=non_overtime+overtime
print(f"Your pay should be ${total_pay:.2f} of which ${overtime:.2f} was overtime pay.")

segments.html: "If" statements are an example of a selection statement. In the overtime example, the program selects and executes the first group of statements after the "if" when the expression following the first "if" is true and the second group when the expression following the second "if" is true. Since only one can be true, only one of these groups of statements are executed.

segments.html: The expression after the "if" is called a Boolean expression because it takes on a value of True or False. Here the expression following the first "if" is "(hours>40)". This will be True if the variable "hours" (input by the user) is greater than 40 and False otherwise.

segments.html: Boolean expressions are named after the nineteenth-century English mathematican George Boole who developed Boolean algebra, which defined the True and False values and the AND, OR and NOT operations that underpin modern computing and the logic used in all computer languages, including Python. In the computer, True is represented by a value of 1 and False with a value of 0.

slides.title: The upper() and lower() string methods

segments.html: The upper() and lower() string methods can be used on a string to convert it to upper or lower case. The syntax is to put a dot after the string and then the method name. (A method is a function that is connected to a type of object, here a string.)
segments.text: The upper() and lower() string methods can be used on a string to convert it to upper or lower case. The syntax is to put a dot after the string and then the method name. (A method is a function that is connected to a type of object, here a string.)

a="aardvark"
z="ZEBRA"
print(a, a.upper())
print(z, z.lower())

if (a.upper()<z):
  print(f'{a.upper()} is less than {z}')

# remember all of the lower case characters are greater than all of the upper case characters
if (a>z):
  print(f'{a} is greater than {z}')

if (a<z.lower()):
  print(f'{a} is less than {z.lower()}')

segments.html: Elif is a way to express additional conditions on the same level as the first "if". Elif is short for "else if." An elif is only run if all the previous conditions have failed to be True. The final "else" is only run if all of the previous conditions have failed. You can have as many elifs as you like.

segments.html: To generate random integers, you first import the random module and then you use the randint method. The randint method takes the two limits of the range of random integers you want (inclusively.)
segments.text: To generate random integers, you first import the random module and then you use the randint method. The randint method takes the two limits of the range of random integers you want (inclusively.)

segments.html: This program picks a random number and then sees if the user can guess it.
segments.text: This program picks a random number and then sees if the user can guess it.

import random
# generate a random integer between 1 and 3
secret=random.randint(1,3)
guess=int(input("What is your guess between 1 and 3?"))
if (guess==secret):
  print("You guessed it!")
else:
  print("Sorry, you didn't guess it.")
